header: Test vectors of type EddsaVerify are intended for testing

CompressedSignature.description: The test vector contains a signature where r and s overlap or where 0 bytes were cut from the signature. This signature was specifically generated.
CompressedSignature.effect: The effect of the bug is unclear without further analysis. It could be rather benign and just allow signature malleability in some cases or it could hide a more severe flaw.

InvalidEncoding.description: The test vector contains a signature with an invalid encoding of the values. The vector checks that invalid encodings are not accepted. For the vectors that modify the encoding of R, S has been recomputed so that the hash matches the modified R and the R recovered from S and the hash equals the original R. Such vectors are accepted only by verifiers that decode R leniently or that compare R to the recovered R incompletely.
InvalidEncoding.effect: Accepting such signatures means the encoding of a signature is not unique. A holder of the private key can generate multiple distinct signatures for the same message, and different verifiers can disagree about which signatures are valid.

InvalidKtv.description: The test vector contains a known invalid signature.

InvalidSignature.description: The test vector contains a signature with edge case values such as 0 or the order of the group.
InvalidSignature.effect: The effect of accepting such signatures probably indicates that signatures can be forged without even knowing the message itself.

Ktv.description: The test vector contains a known valid signature.

SignatureMalleability.description: EdDSA signatures are non-malleable, if implemented correctly. If an implementation fails to check the range of S then it may be possible to modify a signature in such a way that it still verifies. See RFC 8032, Section 5.1.7 and Section 8.4.

SignatureWithGarbage.description: The test vector contains a signature with additional content. EdDSA signature are expected to be non-malleable. Signatures of the wrong length should be rejected. See RFC 8032, Section 5.1.7 and Section 8.4.

TinkOverflow.description: The test vector contains a signature that caused an arithmetic overflow in tink.

TruncatedSignature.description: The test vector contains a signature that was truncated.
TruncatedSignature.effect: Accepting such signatures likely means that signatures can be forged.

Valid.description: The test vector is an ordinary valid signature.

SmallOrderPublicKey.description: The public key is a canonical point in the Ed25519 torsion subgroup. These signatures satisfy the cofactored verification equation in RFC 8032, Section 5.1.7. Implementations may reject them under a stricter public-key policy.
SmallOrderPublicKey.effect: Verifiers with different public-key validation policies may disagree on these signatures.

MixedOrderPublicKey.description: The public key has a nonzero torsion component and is not in the prime-order subgroup. Signatures that satisfy the cofactored verification equation in RFC 8032, Section 5.1.7 are acceptable; implementations may reject them under a stricter subgroup policy. Signatures that fail this equation are invalid.
MixedOrderPublicKey.effect: Verifiers with different subgroup policies may disagree on equation-valid signatures.

the encoded s was replaced by s + p where p is the field prime 2^255 - 19. The scalar differs from the valid s mod L, so verification fails even without a range check on s. Accepted only by verifiers that reduce s mod p instead of checking s < L.
